findings.F1: The move after a break grows with the horizon and goes well past the plan's 5 days. From the first bar of each long bet (1240 starts), the unusual move is +0.95 % over 5 days (t 2.65, strength 0.083), +1.93 % over 10 days (t 3.41, 1192 starts, strength 0.114) and +3.62 % over 20 days (t 3.61, 1111 starts, strength 0.129). The total move over 20 days is +6.04 %, about 30 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: Most of the 20-day move comes after the plan's 5-day bet ends. From day 5 to day 20 after a break start, the unusual move is +1.98 % (t 2.41, 1111 starts). The book's longest-held trades (mean 15.3 days, 421 trades) earn +9.95 % net with 62 % winners, against −0.85 % for trades held about 4.7 days. Starts can overlap, though: kept at least 20 days apart, the same moves are +2.88 % over 20 days and +1.95 % from day 5 to 20, both with t 1.27 to 1.59 on 357 starts. So F1 and F2 are partly inflated by counting nearby starts more than once.

findings.F4: The strongest breaks follow the same pattern as F3. The break's touch count times its margin, top group (mean 8.75), is followed by +0.48 % unusual over 20 days, against +3.1 % to +6.5 % for the lower three groups (about 275 starts each). Spearman is −0.065.
findings.F5: Bear years carry the breaks' losses. Starts kept 20 days apart lose −24.2 % unusual over 20 days in 2018 (t −5.18, 19 starts) and −6.2 % in 2022 (t −1.97, 28 starts). Every other year is positive: +0.7 % to +7.4 %.
findings.F6: Saturday stands out among the weekdays, but it is a fixed calendar condition and I could not grade it.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, while its 60-day return is positive, it keeps rising over the next 20 days, and the more times that level turned it down before, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A break of a repeatedly held level in an uptrend is a reason to hold a long for about three weeks, not five days, since most of the rise comes after the first week and its size far exceeds a trade's cost.
ideas.name: breakout continues three weeks

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, the further its close stands above its 50-day average, the smaller its rise over the next 20 days.
ideas.consequence: A break made from far above the 50-day average is a reason to buy less or not at all, while a break near the average is a reason to buy with full conviction.
ideas.name: overextended breakouts fade
